extracted.intended_audience: individuals and organizations submitting public comments on federal regulations (advocates, attorneys, subject-matter experts, affected stakeholders)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for drafting effective public comments in federal notice-and-comment rulemaking that trigger an agency's legal obligation to respond. Emphasizes legal grounding (5 U.S.C. § 553), specificity, substantive analysis, and practical implementation considerations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Specificity & Evidence
rubrics_metrics.description: Comments must reference the specific regulation being addressed and support positions with factual data, research, or concrete examples rather than general statements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be concrete: cite the exact provision or section, provide data, studies, or concrete examples that substantiate claims. Avoid broad, abstract complaints; specificity increases likelihood the agency will treat the point as a 'significant issue' requiring a response.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clear Position-Taking
rubrics_metrics.description: Commenters should explicitly state whether they support, oppose, or propose modifications, avoiding ambiguous language.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use plain declarative statements (e.g., 'We oppose proposed §X because...'; 'We support with these suggested edits...'). Explicit positions make it easier for agencies to identify issues and explain responses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Substantive Analysis
rubrics_metrics.description: Thorough engagement with the regulatory rationale is essential because agencies must 'respond to all significant issues raised in the comments.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explain why the rule's rationale is flawed or incomplete, directly engage agency reasoning and evidence, and show how your arguments materially bear on the agency's decision-making record.

rubrics_metrics.name: Citations to relevant legal authorities (5 U.S.C. § 553)
rubrics_metrics.description: Does the comment cite 5 U.S.C. § 553 or other governing authority where relevant?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reference applicable statutes, procedural requirements, and controlling case law to frame the comment as legally cognizable and to remind the agency of its statutory obligations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reference to existing studies or precedents
rubrics_metrics.description: Does the comment cite empirical studies or precedents?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide peer-reviewed studies, government reports, or prior agency decisions that support your position; well-sourced evidence helps the agency justify changes and demonstrates the comment's factual basis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Personal expertise or professional qualifications
rubrics_metrics.description: Does the commenter identify their professional or experiential qualifications?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include relevant credentials, professional roles, or lived-experience statements to establish epistemic authority and explain why the commenter is a reliable source on the topic.

rubrics_metrics.name: Specific alternative regulatory text
rubrics_metrics.description: Does the comment propose specific alternative regulatory text?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide concrete drafting suggestions (exact statutory/regulatory language) so the agency has an actionable option to adopt rather than only a critique.

rubrics_metrics.name: Acknowledgment of counterarguments
rubrics_metrics.description: Does the comment acknowledge counterarguments?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Anticipate and respond to likely opposing points to show good-faith engagement and strengthen the persuasiveness and completeness of your analysis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Implementation feasibility and cost discussion
rubrics_metrics.description: Does the comment discuss implementation feasibility and cost?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Address how proposed changes would be implemented, potential costs or burdens, and practical considerations to reduce agency concerns about practicability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Connection between requested changes and statutory requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Does the comment connect requested changes to statutory requirements?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explain how the suggested modifications further statutory purposes or resolve statutory conflicts; tie proposals back to legal mandates and policy objectives the agency must consider.

rubrics_metrics.name: Distinction between opinion and verifiable fact
rubrics_metrics.description: Does the comment distinguish opinion from verifiable fact?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Label normative statements as opinion and support empirical claims with citations or data. Clear separation improves credibility and helps the agency identify record evidence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Logical flow from problem identification to proposed solution
rubrics_metrics.description: Logical flow from problem identification to proposed solution is a structural quality indicator.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Organize comments so they move coherently: define the problem, explain why it matters (with evidence), analyze the rule's shortcomings, and present specific remedies or edits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accessible format, clear organization, professional tone, concise language
rubrics_metrics.description: Accessible format with clear organization, professional tone, and concise language are structural quality indicators.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use headings, short paragraphs, numbered lists, and plain language to make points easy for agency reviewers to locate and understand; maintain civility and professionalism to preserve credibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rubric checklist item: cite 5 U.S.C. § 553 or other governing authority
rubrics_metrics.description: Does the comment cite 5 U.S.C. § 553 or other governing authority where relevant? (checklist item)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explicitly citing the statute helps frame legal arguments and signals that the comment raises issues the agency may be legally obliged to address.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rubric checklist item: cite empirical studies or precedents
rubrics_metrics.description: Does the comment cite empirical studies or precedents? (checklist item)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Empirical and precedent citations bolster factual and legal claims and make it easier for the agency to incorporate or rebut evidence in the rulemaking record.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rubric checklist item: identify professional or experiential qualifications
rubrics_metrics.description: Does the commenter identify their professional or experiential qualifications? (checklist item)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clear credentials increase the persuasive weight of technical assertions and help the agency assess the reliability of the submitted evidence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rubric checklist item: propose specific alternative regulatory text
rubrics_metrics.description: Does the comment propose specific alternative regulatory text? (checklist item)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Providing draft regulatory language reduces drafting burden on the agency and increases the likelihood your proposal can be adopted verbatim or adapted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rubric checklist item: acknowledge counterarguments
rubrics_metrics.description: Does the comment acknowledge counterarguments? (checklist item)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Acknowledging and rebutting counterarguments demonstrates comprehensiveness and good-faith engagement, which can strengthen the agency's obligation to respond.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rubric checklist item: discuss implementation feasibility and cost
rubrics_metrics.description: Does the comment discuss implementation feasibility and cost? (checklist item)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Addressing costs and feasibility preempts agency concerns about practicability and helps the agency evaluate the reasonableness of proposed changes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rubric checklist item: connect requested changes to statutory requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Does the comment connect requested changes to statutory requirements? (checklist item)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explicit statutory linkage clarifies how the suggested modifications further legal duties or correct statutory inconsistencies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rubric checklist item: distinguish opinion from verifiable fact
rubrics_metrics.description: Does the comment distinguish opinion from verifiable fact? (checklist item)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mark normative claims as opinion and back factual claims with citations to ensure agency reviewers can readily identify evidentiary material in the record.
